keyProjects.description: Sensor CMOS de ultra-baja iluminación con filtro IR retirado, iluminador VCSEL de 940nm y micro-display OLED.

benchCalibration: Paso 1: Test de Continuidad en Frío: Con el multímetro en modo pitido/continuidad y el circuito completamente apagado, comprobar que no hay conexión entre el riel de alimentación VCC y la masa GND.

Paso 2: Primer Encendido Protegido: Ajustar la fuente de laboratorio a la tensión nominal (ej. 3.3V o 5.0V) y limitar la corriente a 150 mA. Si la fuente entra en modo corriente constante (CC), desconectar inmediatamente y buscar puentes de estaño.

Paso 3: Escaneo de Direcciones de Bus: Ejecutar un script de escáner de bus (ej. I2C Scanner) y confirmar que el módulo responde en su dirección hexadecimal exacta (ej. 0x68 para MPU, 0x28 para BNO, 0x40 para INA219).

Paso 4: Calibración de Sesgo Estático (Zero-Motion Offset): Dejar el dispositivo inmóvil sobre el banco de trabajo durante 10 segundos. El firmware promediará 1000 muestras para calcular y restar el offset inicial de los sensores.
Paso 5: Prueba de Esfuerzo y Termografía: Hacer funcionar el dispositivo a plena carga durante 15 minutos comprobando con termómetro de infrarrojos que ningún chip supere los 60°C.
consoleCommands: # Actualizar dependencias de vídeo y librerías de visión
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y python3-opencv python3-picamera2 libcamera-tools
# Probar funcionamiento del sensor infrarrojo sin filtro
libcamera-hello -t 5000 --tuning-file /usr/share/libcamera/ipa/rpi/vc4/imx708_noir.json
# Iniciar script de baja latencia a pantalla completa
python3 -u night_vision_stream.py --gain 16.0 --exposure 33000 --fps 30
detailedBuildManual.firmwareCode:
// Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
mechanicalSteps: Mecanizado o Impresión 3D del Soporte: Imprimir el chasis con filamento PETG o ABS con un 35% de relleno giroide para maximizar la rigidez y minimizar resonancias mecánicas.

Aislamiento de Vibraciones: Emplear 'dampers' o arandelas de silicona suave en los 4 puntos de anclaje de la placa del sensor para filtrar armónicos de alta frecuencia provocados por motores o ventiladores.

Orientación Geométrica: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance del dispositivo. Una desviación angular de tan solo 2° introduce un error de deriva de aceleración cruzada.
Disipación Térmica: Si la etapa de conmutación disipa más de 1W, montar un disipador de aluminio anodizado con adhesivo térmico de 1.5 W/m-K.

troubleshooting.cause: Falta de resistencias pull-up externas en las líneas SDA/SCL, o capacitancia parásita por cables demasiado largos (> 15 cm).
troubleshooting.fix: Soldar dos resistencias pull-up de 4.7 kΩ entre SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V. Acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm y trenzarlos junto con una línea de masa GND para blindaje.
troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se bloquea de forma intermitente.

troubleshooting.cause: Pico de corriente transitorio (inrush current) que provoca una caída momentánea del voltaje por debajo de 2.7V en el regulador.
troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico Low-ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con la entrada de alimentación y desacoplar la etapa lógica con un diodo Schottky y condensador dedicado.
troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicio espontáneo del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al activarse actuadores o transmisores RF.

troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento capacitivo o inductivo generado por cables de motor PWM que discurren en paralelo a las líneas de datos de señal débil.
troubleshooting.fix: Separar físicamente los cables de potencia de los cables de señal al menos 3 cm, o utilizar cable apantallado con la malla conectada a masa sólo en un extremo.
troubleshooting.symptom: La señal del sensor muestra oscilaciones caóticas o ruido de alta frecuencia.

troubleshooting.cause: Variación térmica en el sensor no compensada o presencia de masa magnética ferrosa cercana (tornillos de acero cerca del magnetómetro).
troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar tornillos de acero por tornillos de latón o nylon amagnéticos, y activar la compensación térmica por software en el firmware.
troubleshooting.symptom: Desviación continua (drift) en la lectura acumulada en reposo.

wiringSteps: Conectar el cable de cinta plana (FPC) de 15 pines del sensor NoIR (Sony Starvis) al puerto CSI del procesador (Raspberry Pi Zero 2W / SBC), asegurando que los contactos metálicos apunten hacia el circuito integrado.
Soldar un cable rojo de 24 AWG desde el pin 1 (3.3V) del microcontrolador al pin VCC de la micropantalla OLED de 0.39 pulgadas.
Soldar un cable negro de 24 AWG desde el pin 6 (GND) del microcontrolador al pin GND de la pantalla y al cátodo del iluminador VCSEL.
Conectar la línea SPI MOSI (Pin 19) al pin DIN de la pantalla para el volcado del buffer de vídeo a 40 MHz.
Conectar la línea SPI SCK (Pin 23) al pin CLK de la micropantalla OLED.

Conectar el pin GPIO 18 (salida PWM) a la puerta (Gate) del transistor MOSFET IRLML2502 a través de una resistencia limitadora de 100 Ω para controlar la potencia del iluminador VCSEL infrarrojo sin sobrecalentar el chip.

officialData.jobMapping: electro-optical (EO/IR) and imaging-systems engineering — night-vision, surveillance-camera, and imaging-sensor teams.
officialData.safety: , NOT SOMEONE ELSE'S Night vision lets you see people who can’t see you. Use it on your own property, on hikes, for wildlife, for astronomy — never to watch people who don’t know you’re there. And keep illuminators to low-power IR LEDs: high-power IR lasers or arrays can injure eyes precisely because you can’t see them.
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand silicon sensor spectral response (why cameras see near-IR), active versus passive illumination, IR illuminator design and
officialData.whyThisMatters: Night vision is the original force multiplier: the side that can see in the dark owns the night. Real image-intensifier tubes cost thousands, but a digital version is astonishingly cheap — a camera with its infrared filter removed sees near-IR light your eyes cannot, and an IR illuminator floods the scene with light that is invisible to everyone but your sensor. Build it into a monocular with a small display and you can walk through a pitch-black room, read a sign at 30 metres, and watch wildlife that has no idea it is lit. It is a beginner build with a jaw- dropping demo, and it teaches the sensor and optics fundamentals behind every EO/IR system. see everything coming — a Build List field guide 2 / 18 --- PAGE 3 ---

officialData.jobMapping: AR / HUD, wearable-systems, and human-machine-interface engineering — defense-headset, avionics-HUD, and AR-hardware teams.
officialData.safety: , and it must never be worn while driving, cycling, or in traffic. Keep most of the field of view clear: a HUD is an aid, not a replacement for looking.
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand optical see-through display design (beam splitters, collimation, eye relief), heading and position sensing (IMU + magnetometer + GPS), rendering a stable HUD from sensor data, and designing information for a glanceable display — the core of AR/HUD and wearable- systems engineering.
officialData.whyThisMatters: The most talked-about piece of modern soldier equipment is the augmented-reality headset: a see- through display that overlays a compass, waypoints, teammate locations, and sensor alerts onto the real world, so the wearer never looks down at a map. You can build the core of one. A small bright display reflected off a half-mirror in front of your eye gives you a see-through HUD; an IMU compass and a GPS feed it heading and position; a radio brings in teammate positions and alerts. Turn your head and the bearing to the waypoint slides across your view. It is optics, embedded systems, and UI design in one build, and the first-person footage is unlike anything else in this series. see everything coming — a Build List field guide 5 / 18 --- PAGE 6 ---

// Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

// Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

officialData.safety: , watching the data in your ground station. Make the first hover low, in a large clear room, with a hand on the sticks and nobody else inside — and never over people. That rule applies to every
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand optical flow (velocity from image motion), why flow must be scaled by height, how a flight controller’s estimator fuses a new sensor, and how to configure and validate that fusion safely. That is the core of GPS-denied navigation.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Outdoors, GPS tells the flight controller where the drone is. Indoors there is no GPS, and a drone drifts like a balloon in a draft. The fix is the same trick an optical mouse uses: a tiny downward camera (a PMW3901 optical-flow sensor) watches the floor texture slide by and reports velocity, while a rangefinder gives height. Feed both to the flight controller and it holds position — a hover you can let go of, indoors, that stays put. It is the cheapest, most dramatic upgrade there is, and it is the foundation for every kind of indoor autonomy. drone upgrades — a Build List field guide 2 / 16 --- PAGE 3 ---

officialData.safety: , NOT A PILOT Avoidance has blind spots (between sensors, above, below) and hard limits (glass, bright sun, speed). Test it slowly, low, in a clear space with a spotter, and never treat it as permission to fly near people. It catches mistakes; it does not replace the pilot.
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand multi-sensor proximity sensing, sector-based obstacle representation, streaming sensor data to a flight controller over a standard protocol, and how avoidance behaviour (stop versus slide,
officialData.whyThisMatters: A drone that can feel the walls is a fundamentally safer drone. Mount a ring of time-of-flight distance sensors around the frame, have a small microcontroller stream the nearest obstacle in each direction to the flight controller as proximity data, and the controller’s own avoidance logic takes over: fly toward a wall and the drone stops short, or slides along it, no matter what the sticks say. Push it toward a doorway and it refuses to hit the frame. It is the flagship of this guide — sensing, integration, and control behaviour in one upgrade — and it is the same layered safety architecture real autonomous drones use. drone upgrades — a Build List field guide 4 / 16 --- PAGE 5 ---

// Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
mechanicalSteps: Mecanizado o Impresión 3D del Soporte: Imprimir el chasis con filamento PETG o ABS con un 35% de relleno giroide para maximizar la rigidez y minimizar resonancias mecánicas.

Aislamiento de Vibraciones: Emplear 'dampers' o arandelas de silicona suave en los 4 puntos de anclaje de la placa del sensor para filtrar armónicos de alta frecuencia provocados por motores o ventiladores.

Orientación Geométrica: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance del dispositivo. Una desviación angular de tan solo 2° introduce un error de deriva de aceleración cruzada.
Disipación Térmica: Si la etapa de conmutación disipa más de 1W, montar un disipador de aluminio anodizado con adhesivo térmico de 1.5 W/m-K.

troubleshooting.cause: Falta de resistencias pull-up externas en las líneas SDA/SCL, o capacitancia parásita por cables demasiado largos (> 15 cm).
troubleshooting.fix: Soldar dos resistencias pull-up de 4.7 kΩ entre SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V. Acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm y trenzarlos junto con una línea de masa GND para blindaje.
troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se bloquea de forma intermitente.

troubleshooting.cause: Pico de corriente transitorio (inrush current) que provoca una caída momentánea del voltaje por debajo de 2.7V en el regulador.
troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico Low-ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con la entrada de alimentación y desacoplar la etapa lógica con un diodo Schottky y condensador dedicado.
troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicio espontáneo del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al activarse actuadores o transmisores RF.

troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento capacitivo o inductivo generado por cables de motor PWM que discurren en paralelo a las líneas de datos de señal débil.
troubleshooting.fix: Separar físicamente los cables de potencia de los cables de señal al menos 3 cm, o utilizar cable apantallado con la malla conectada a masa sólo en un extremo.
troubleshooting.symptom: La señal del sensor muestra oscilaciones caóticas o ruido de alta frecuencia.

troubleshooting.cause: Variación térmica en el sensor no compensada o presencia de masa magnética ferrosa cercana (tornillos de acero cerca del magnetómetro).
troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar tornillos de acero por tornillos de latón o nylon amagnéticos, y activar la compensación térmica por software en el firmware.
troubleshooting.symptom: Desviación continua (drift) en la lectura acumulada en reposo.

wiringSteps: Conectar el cable de cinta plana (FPC) de 15 pines del sensor NoIR (Sony Starvis) al puerto CSI del procesador (Raspberry Pi Zero 2W / SBC), asegurando que los contactos metálicos apunten hacia el circuito integrado.
Soldar un cable rojo de 24 AWG desde el pin 1 (3.3V) del microcontrolador al pin VCC de la micropantalla OLED de 0.39 pulgadas.
Soldar un cable negro de 24 AWG desde el pin 6 (GND) del microcontrolador al pin GND de la pantalla y al cátodo del iluminador VCSEL.
Conectar la línea SPI MOSI (Pin 19) al pin DIN de la pantalla para el volcado del buffer de vídeo a 40 MHz.
Conectar la línea SPI SCK (Pin 23) al pin CLK de la micropantalla OLED.

Conectar el pin GPIO 18 (salida PWM) a la puerta (Gate) del transistor MOSFET IRLML2502 a través de una resistencia limitadora de 100 Ω para controlar la potencia del iluminador VCSEL infrarrojo sin sobrecalentar el chip.

officialData.whyThisMatters: Motors fail, batteries fail, and a drone that loses power becomes a falling brick. A parachute recovery system detects the fall — or takes a command — kills the motors, and deploys a canopy so the aircraft comes down at a walking pace instead of terminal velocity. Commercial systems cost hundreds; you can build one with a spring-loaded tube, a servo pin, an accelerometer, and a properly sized canopy. // Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
mechanicalSteps: Mecanizado o Impresión 3D del Soporte: Imprimir el chasis con filamento PETG o ABS con un 35% de relleno giroide para maximizar la rigidez y minimizar resonancias mecánicas.

Aislamiento de Vibraciones: Emplear 'dampers' o arandelas de silicona suave en los 4 puntos de anclaje de la placa del sensor para filtrar armónicos de alta frecuencia provocados por motores o ventiladores.

Orientación Geométrica: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance del dispositivo. Una desviación angular de tan solo 2° introduce un error de deriva de aceleración cruzada.
Disipación Térmica: Si la etapa de conmutación disipa más de 1W, montar un disipador de aluminio anodizado con adhesivo térmico de 1.5 W/m-K.

troubleshooting.cause: Falta de resistencias pull-up externas en las líneas SDA/SCL, o capacitancia parásita por cables demasiado largos (> 15 cm).
troubleshooting.fix: Soldar dos resistencias pull-up de 4.7 kΩ entre SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V. Acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm y trenzarlos junto con una línea de masa GND para blindaje.
troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se bloquea de forma intermitente.

troubleshooting.cause: Pico de corriente transitorio (inrush current) que provoca una caída momentánea del voltaje por debajo de 2.7V en el regulador.
troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico Low-ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con la entrada de alimentación y desacoplar la etapa lógica con un diodo Schottky y condensador dedicado.
troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicio espontáneo del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al activarse actuadores o transmisores RF.

troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento capacitivo o inductivo generado por cables de motor PWM que discurren en paralelo a las líneas de datos de señal débil.
troubleshooting.fix: Separar físicamente los cables de potencia de los cables de señal al menos 3 cm, o utilizar cable apantallado con la malla conectada a masa sólo en un extremo.
troubleshooting.symptom: La señal del sensor muestra oscilaciones caóticas o ruido de alta frecuencia.

troubleshooting.cause: Variación térmica en el sensor no compensada o presencia de masa magnética ferrosa cercana (tornillos de acero cerca del magnetómetro).
troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar tornillos de acero por tornillos de latón o nylon amagnéticos, y activar la compensación térmica por software en el firmware.
troubleshooting.symptom: Desviación continua (drift) en la lectura acumulada en reposo.

wiringSteps: Conectar el cable de cinta plana (FPC) de 15 pines del sensor NoIR (Sony Starvis) al puerto CSI del procesador (Raspberry Pi Zero 2W / SBC), asegurando que los contactos metálicos apunten hacia el circuito integrado.
Soldar un cable rojo de 24 AWG desde el pin 1 (3.3V) del microcontrolador al pin VCC de la micropantalla OLED de 0.39 pulgadas.
Soldar un cable negro de 24 AWG desde el pin 6 (GND) del microcontrolador al pin GND de la pantalla y al cátodo del iluminador VCSEL.

// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")
mechanicalSteps: Mecanizado o Impresión 3D del Soporte: Imprimir el chasis con filamento PETG o ABS con un 35% de relleno giroide para maximizar la rigidez y minimizar resonancias mecánicas.

Orientación Geométrica: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance del dispositivo. Una desviación angular de tan solo 2° introduce un error de deriva de aceleración cruzada.

Verificar que la malla exterior del conector SMA esté conectada al plano de tierra general de la estación.

// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")
mechanicalSteps: Mecanizado o Impresión 3D del Soporte: Imprimir el chasis con filamento PETG o ABS con un 35% de relleno giroide para maximizar la rigidez y minimizar resonancias mecánicas.

Aislamiento de Vibraciones: Emplear 'dampers' o arandelas de silicona suave en los 4 puntos de anclaje de la placa del sensor para filtrar armónicos de alta frecuencia provocados por motores o ventiladores.

Orientación Geométrica: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance del dispositivo. Una desviación angular de tan solo 2° introduce un error de deriva de aceleración cruzada.
Disipación Térmica: Si la etapa de conmutación disipa más de 1W, montar un disipador de aluminio anodizado con adhesivo térmico de 1.5 W/m-K.

// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

// Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

detailedBuildManual.firmwareCode:
// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

officialData.whatThisProves: You understand H-bridge topology, PWM speed control, motor direction switching, freewheeling and why inductive loads need it, and current sensing — the power-stage foundation of motor-drive and robotics hardware.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Before a robot can balance, drive, or steer, something has to turn a control signal into torque. An H-bridge does exactly that: four switches that push current through a DC motor in either direction, plus PWM that sets how hard. Build one, drive a motor forward and reverse, ramp its speed smoothly, and sense the current it draws, and you have the power stage that sits under every motor-control project in this guide. It is the cheapest, most fundamental motor build, and the payoff is immediate — a motor that does exactly what your code says.

detailedBuildManual.firmwareCode:
// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")
mechanicalSteps: Mecanizado o Impresión 3D del Soporte: Imprimir el chasis con filamento PETG o ABS con un 35% de relleno giroide para maximizar la rigidez y minimizar resonancias mecánicas.

Aislamiento de Vibraciones: Emplear 'dampers' o arandelas de silicona suave en los 4 puntos de anclaje de la placa del sensor para filtrar armónicos de alta frecuencia provocados por motores o ventiladores.

Orientación Geométrica: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance del dispositivo. Una desviación angular de tan solo 2° introduce un error de deriva de aceleración cruzada.
Disipación Térmica: Si la etapa de conmutación disipa más de 1W, montar un disipador de aluminio anodizado con adhesivo térmico de 1.5 W/m-K.

troubleshooting.cause: Falta de resistencias pull-up externas en las líneas SDA/SCL, o capacitancia parásita por cables demasiado largos (> 15 cm).
troubleshooting.fix: Soldar dos resistencias pull-up de 4.7 kΩ entre SDA/SCL y el riel de 3.3V. Acortar los cables a menos de 10 cm y trenzarlos junto con una línea de masa GND para blindaje.
troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se bloquea de forma intermitente.

troubleshooting.cause: Pico de corriente transitorio (inrush current) que provoca una caída momentánea del voltaje por debajo de 2.7V en el regulador.
troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico Low-ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con la entrada de alimentación y desacoplar la etapa lógica con un diodo Schottky y condensador dedicado.
troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicio espontáneo del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al activarse actuadores o transmisores RF.

troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento capacitivo o inductivo generado por cables de motor PWM que discurren en paralelo a las líneas de datos de señal débil.
troubleshooting.fix: Separar físicamente los cables de potencia de los cables de señal al menos 3 cm, o utilizar cable apantallado con la malla conectada a masa sólo en un extremo.
troubleshooting.symptom: La señal del sensor muestra oscilaciones caóticas o ruido de alta frecuencia.

troubleshooting.cause: Variación térmica en el sensor no compensada o presencia de masa magnética ferrosa cercana (tornillos de acero cerca del magnetómetro).
troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar tornillos de acero por tornillos de latón o nylon amagnéticos, y activar la compensación térmica por software en el firmware.
troubleshooting.symptom: Desviación continua (drift) en la lectura acumulada en reposo.

wiringSteps: Conectar el receptor RTL-SDR Blog v4 al puerto USB con apantallamiento para evitar que el ruido del bus USB degrade la relación señal/ruido (SNR).

Conectar la antena monopolo o dipolo telescópico sintonizada a la frecuencia de interés mediante conector SMA macho de 50 Ω (longitud de antena L = 300 / F_MHz / 4 metros; ej. 6.8 cm para ADS-B 1090 MHz).
Si se emplea un filtro SAW y LNA (Low-Noise Amplifier), intercalarlo entre la antena y la entrada SMA activando la alimentación Bias-Tee (4.5V DC por el cable coaxial).
Conectar la interfaz I2C del microcontrolador auxiliar (SDA GPIO 21, SCL GPIO 22) para telemetría de espectro y alertas sonoras.
Verificar que la malla exterior del conector SMA esté conectada al plano de tierra general de la estación.

officialData.whyThisMatters: A two-wheel balancing robot is an inverted pendulum: left alone it falls, so it only stays upright because a controller is constantly catching it. If the closed-loop servo taught you to hold a position, this teaches you to stabilise something that actively wants to fall.

officialData.safety: Desconectar la alimentación antes de modificar el cableado. Verificar ausencia de cortocircuitos entre 3.3V y GND con multímetro antes de energizar.
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand three-phase brushless motors, electronic commutation, the idea of FOC (Clarke / Park transforms, controlling torque-producing current directly), rotor position sensing, and three-phase driver hardware — core to motor-drive, drone, EV, and robotics-actuator engineering.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Brushless (BLDC / PMSM) motors are everywhere high performance matters — drones, EVs, robot joints, gimbals — because they are efficient, powerful, and long-lived. But they need electronic commutation: you must energise the right coils at the right instant based on rotor position. Field-Oriented Control (FOC) does this optimally, producing smooth, silent, full- torque-at-any-speed motion, even holding still. Building a FOC drive — with a position sensor, a three-phase driver, and a library like SimpleFOC — is the leap into modern motor control and one of the most in-demand EE skills in robotics and electrified everything.

// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

officialData.whyThisMatters: Most knobs are passive; this one fights back. By driving a brushless motor with FOC and reading its exact angle, you can render torque as a function of position — so the same physical knob can feel like clicky detents, a smooth spring that returns to centre, or a hard end-stop, all changed in software. It is the technology behind high-end car controls and the viral “smart knob,” and it is a brilliant lesson in torque control and haptics: you are programming a force field you can feel with your fingers. It builds directly on FOC and turns motor control into a user interface.

// Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

officialData.jobMapping: Flight controls / GNC engineer — attitude estimation and inner-loop stabilization for multirotors. SAFETY WARNING Run every test with propellers removed until the rig is stable on the stand; a loop that saturates will spin motors to full throttle without warning.
officialData.safety: Desconectar la alimentación antes de modificar el cableado. Verificar ausencia de cortocircuitos entre 3.3V y GND con multímetro antes de energizar.
officialData.whatThisProves: You can explain where your angle estimate comes from, why you fused gyro and accelerometer instead of trusting either, what your loop rate is and why, and what the D-term does when the motor response is slow. You tuned gains on real hardware with a logged step response, not a slider in a simulator. That is a control-systems story a drone company can check in one question — and almost no one walks in with it.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Every drone company assumes a graduate has only ever flashed Betaflight, and that assumption is usually correct. This project forces you through the part the firmware hides: raw gyro rates and accelerometer vectors coming in at 1 kHz, a complementary (or Kalman) filter turning them into a roll and pitch angle, and a PID loop turning that angle error into motor commands. You will discover that the textbook loop oscillates on a real rig, that the gyro drifts, that the accelerometer lies under vibration, and that the difference between a stable hover and a flip is a derivative term and a 100 Hz low-pass filter. Debugging that on a hinged one-axis test stand, with a logged plot of setpoint versus measured angle, is the actual skill a flight-controls engineer is hired for.

officialData.whatThisProves: You can draw a three-phase bridge from memory, explain dead-time and shoot-through, describe how zero-crossing detection works and why it fails at low speed, and show a scope capture of your own commutation. officialData.whyThisMatters: An ESC is a black box to most EE students: a $12 brick that turns a PWM signal into a spinning motor. Inside it is a three-phase half-bridge, gate drivers, a microcontroller and a way of finding the rotor without sensors — by watching the back-EMF zero crossing on the floating phase. Building it yourself means you will blow a MOSFET by shooting through a half-bridge, you will see the back-EMF on a scope and learn why it only appears once the motor is already turning, and you will write an open-loop start-up ramp that hands off to sensorless commutation. That is the exact circuit inside every motor controller in the industry, and the debugging — dead time, gate charge, current spikes — is the actual job.

// Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

picam2.set_controls({

})

cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")

    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad

officialData.jobMapping: Battery / power systems engineer — BMS, power monitoring and energy estimation for electric aircraft. SAFETY WARNING Never leave a LiPo connected to a discharge load unattended, and stop any test the moment a cell reads under 3.0 V — over-discharged cells are the ones that catch fire on the next charge.
officialData.safety: Desconectar la alimentación antes de modificar el cableado. Verificar ausencia de cortocircuitos entre 3.3V y GND con multímetro antes de energizar.
officialData.whatThisProves: You can explain high-side versus low-side current sensing, size a shunt for a 60 A pack, talk about coulomb counting versus voltage estimation, and show a discharge curve with a weak cell visible in it. That is battery-management experience, and 'BMS' shows up in nearly every drone, EV and robotics hardware posting.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Batteries decide flight time and batteries cause crashes, so every drone company has someone who owns the power module. This project is that module: a shunt resistor and current-sense amplifier for pack current, a resistor-divider per cell into a multiplexed ADC for cell voltages, and firmware that integrates current into mAh consumed and flags a weak cell. You will learn why a 0.5 m� shunt needs a 50 V/V amplifier, why the divider ratio matters for ADC resolution, why cell voltage under load and at rest are different numbers, and why mAh consumed is a better land-now signal than voltage. The logged discharge curve you produce is the first thing a battery engineer asks for.

// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

officialData.jobMapping: Localization / navigation engineer — GPS-denied positioning and sensor fusion for indoor UAS.
officialData.safety: Desconectar la alimentación antes de modificar el cableado. Verificar ausencia de cortocircuitos entre 3.3V y GND con multímetro antes de energizar.
officialData.whatThisProves: You can explain two-way ranging and why it cancels clock offset, what limits UWB accuracy indoors (antenna delay, multipath, geometry), how trilateration degrades when anchors are nearly collinear, and you have a plot of a walked square that looks like a square. Localization and sensor fusion are exactly what indoor-drone companies screen for — and this build is the first rung of it.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Indoor drones are the fastest-growing part of the industry — warehouse inventory, tunnel and tank inspection — and none of them have GPS. This project is the answer those teams actually use: ultra-wideband ranging. Three ESP32 + DW1000 anchors on tripods, one tag on the airframe, two-way ranging that times a radio pulse round trip to nanoseconds, and trilateration that turns three distances into an x/y position on a laptop map. You will learn why UWB can range to centimetres when WiFi cannot, why antenna delay calibration is the whole game, and why three anchors give you a position but four give you a sanity check. The logged position trace as you walk a square is proof you can build a localization system, not just call a library.

These are the exact skills behind satellite communications, GPS, radar, and every space-to-ground link in the industry. --- PAGE 3 --- @1nska • 6 EE Projects That Reach Space • Page 3 How It Works • Geostationary downlink (1.69 GHz): GOES-East (GOES-19) and GOES-West (GOES-18) broadcast HRIT near 1694.1 MHz. The signal is BPSK at roughly 400 kSym/s and carries full-disk Earth images, regional mesoscale scans, and weather products. • Antenna — gain is everything: After a 36,000 km path the signal is extremely weak, so you need directional gain. A repurposed 2.4 GHz WiFi grid dish, a small offset satellite dish with a helical feed, or a DIY cookware reflector all work. Because the bird is geostationary, you point once and bolt it down. • Low-noise amplifier + SAW filter: An LNA with a sub-1 dB noise figure, mounted right at the antenna feed, sets the system sensitivity. A SAW filter near 1.69 GHz rejects cellular and WiFi that would otherwise desensitize the receiver. This LNA-at-the-antenna placement is the single most important decision in the build. • Bias tee + SDR: A bias tee injects DC up the coax to power the LNA at the mast while passing RF down to the radio. An RTL-SDR (or Airspy for more headroom) digitizes the filtered signal and streams IQ samples to a laptop or Raspberry Pi. • Demodulation + decode (SatDump): SatDump locks the BPSK carrier, recovers symbol timing, applies Viterbi and Reed-Solomon forward error correction, and reassembles the packets into full-disk and mesoscale images — the same pictures meteorologists use, pulled out of the air by you. // Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

Aislamiento de Vibraciones: Emplear 'dampers' o arandelas de silicona suave en los 4 puntos de anclaje de la placa del sensor para filtrar armónicos de alta frecuencia provocados por motores o ventiladores.

troubleshooting.fix: Soldar un condensador electrolítico Low-ESR de 470 µF a 1000 µF en paralelo con la entrada de alimentación y desacoplar la etapa lógica con un diodo Schottky y condensador dedicado.
troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicio espontáneo del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al activarse actuadores o transmisores RF.

troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento capacitivo o inductivo generado por cables de motor PWM que discurren en paralelo a las líneas de datos de señal débil.

officialData.whatThisProves: : You understand VHF reception, antenna design and polarization (why satellites use circular polarization), Doppler shift, and digital QPSK demodulation with forward error correction — the same RF fundamentals that scale all the way up to GOES and deep-space communication. --- PAGE 7 --- @1nska • 6 EE Projects That Reach Space • Page 7 How It Works • Polar LRPT downlink (137 MHz): Meteor-M2-3 and M2-4 transmit LRPT near 137.9 MHz (137.1 MHz backup). Unlike the old analog NOAA APT, LRPT is digital QPSK at about 72 kbps, carrying a crisper multi-spectral image. • A satellite that moves: These satellites orbit roughly 800 km up in a sun-synchronous polar orbit, crossing your sky in about 12–15 minutes per pass. You capture a strip of Earth directly under the ground track — typically your region and a few hundred km either side. • Antenna and polarization: A V-dipole (two ~50 cm wires at about 120 degrees) is the simplest antenna; a QFH (quadrifilar helix) is omnidirectional and better for the ever-changing pass geometry. Satellites transmit circular polarization, which is why a QFH outperforms a flat dipole on low passes. • Optional LNA for the city: In a quiet rural spot the SDR alone can decode a high pass. In a city full of RF noise, a 137 MHz SAW-filtered LNA at the antenna dramatically improves results by rejecting pagers, FM broadcast, and other interference. • Doppler and decode (SatDump): Because the satellite is moving fast, its frequency shifts by several kHz across the pass (Doppler). SatDump tracks the satellite by its orbital elements, corrects Doppler, demodulates the QPSK, applies error correction, and assembles the decoded image. // Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

officialData.whatThisProves: : You understand closed-loop control (PID/LQR), sensor fusion, BLDC motor torque control, and real-time embedded firmware. Attitude determination and control is a core aerospace discipline, and the same fundamentals underpin robotics, drones, and self-balancing vehicles. --- PAGE 10 --- @1nska • 6 EE Projects That Reach Space • Page 10 How It Works • Conservation of angular momentum: The platform sits on a low-friction bearing. When the motor accelerates the flywheel clockwise, the platform reacts by rotating counter-clockwise. The torque on the body equals the rate of change of the wheel's angular momentum — so wheel acceleration is your control input. • IMU attitude sensing: An MPU-6050 or BNO055 IMU fuses its gyroscope and accelerometer to estimate the platform's tilt angle and angular rate. A complementary or Kalman filter blends the drift-free-but-noisy accelerometer with the smooth-but-drifting gyro. • The control loop: A PID (or LQR) controller takes the angle error and computes a commanded wheel torque. For the balancing-pendulum version it must stabilize an inherently unstable equilibrium — like balancing a broom on your palm, but a thousand times a second. • BLDC torque control: A brushless gimbal motor spins the flywheel. A field-oriented control (FOC) driver regulates motor current, and since torque is proportional to current, this gives direct, smooth torque control — far better than crude PWM speed control. • Momentum saturation: If the platform keeps disturbing in one direction, the wheel spins faster and faster until it hits its limit — saturation. Real satellites dump this momentum with magnetorquers or thrusters. On the bench you will watch the wheel max out and learn why momentum management matters. officialData.whatThisProves: : You understand low-light image sensors and optics (f-number, exposure), embedded computer vision, star-identification algorithms, and the coordinate-frame math (quaternions) behind pointing systems. Star trackers are flagship aerospace GNC hardware — building one signals you can work on real spacecraft guidance. --- PAGE 13 --- @1nska • 6 EE Projects That Reach Space • Page 13 How It Works • Fast lens + low-light sensor: Stars are dim, so the optics matter most. A fast lens (f/1.4–f/2) gathers maximum light; a sensitive CMOS sensor (a Raspberry Pi HQ camera or a Sony IMX module) with a multi-second exposure captures enough stars per frame to identify a pattern. Monochrome and longer exposure both help. • Star centroiding: The software thresholds the image to separate stars from background, then computes the sub-pixel centroid of each star blob. Centroiding to a fraction of a pixel is what gives the tracker its arc-second accuracy — far finer than the pixel grid itself. • Pattern matching (lost in space): The key trick: the angular distances between stars form a unique fingerprint. An open-source solver like Tetra3 hashes these geometric patterns and matches them against a precomputed catalog — identifying exactly which stars you are looking at with no prior orientation estimate. • Attitude solve: Once stars are identified, their known catalog positions (right ascension and declination) plus their measured pixel positions let the solver compute the rotation that maps one to the other. The result is the camera's orientation, expressed as a quaternion or rotation matrix. • Edge compute: All of this runs on a Raspberry Pi (Zero 2 W or Pi 4). The solve takes well under a second per frame — fast enough to output a continuous attitude estimate, exactly as a real star tracker feeds a spacecraft's control system. // Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

officialData.whatThisProves: : You understand precision frequency references, phase-locked control loops, GNSS timing (1PPS), oscillator steering via DAC or varactor, and how to characterize stability with Allan deviation. Timing and synchronization is foundational to communications, radar, and instrumentation — and surprisingly few engineers actually understand it. --- PAGE 16 --- @1nska • 6 EE Projects That Reach Space • Page 16 How It Works • The 1PPS reference: A GPS receiver outputs a one-pulse-per-second signal whose rising edge is aligned to GPS system time — itself steered by the atomic clocks aboard the satellites. The edge is accurate to tens of nanoseconds, but it jitters pulse-to-pulse, so it is a great long-term reference and a poor short-term one. • The local oscillator: An OCXO (oven-controlled crystal oscillator) is extremely stable second-to-second but slowly drifts over hours and temperature. It is the opposite of GPS: great short-term, poor long-term. The whole idea is to combine the two. • Phase comparison: The MCU divides the OCXO (e.g. 10 MHz) down to 1 Hz and measures the time error between that and the GPS 1PPS using a hardware timer's input capture. This error, in nanoseconds, is the signal the control loop drives to zero. • The loop filter: A slow software control loop — a long time constant of many seconds to minutes — averages out the GPS jitter and computes a correction. Too fast and you chase GPS noise; too slow and you fail to track drift. This tradeoff is the heart of the design. • Steering the oscillator: The correction drives a DAC that sets the OCXO's electronic frequency control (EFC) voltage, nudging it a few parts-per-billion. Over minutes the loop converges and the OCXO is disciplined — its frequency now traceable to the same standard as the satellites overhead. // Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

officialData.whatThisProves: : You understand SiPM biasing and temperature compensation, low-noise transimpedance amplification, fast pulse discrimination, and coincidence detection. This is high-speed, low-noise analog at the edge of what is possible — exactly the skill set behind medical imaging, LIDAR, and scientific instrumentation. --- PAGE 19 --- @1nska • 6 EE Projects That Reach Space • Page 19 How It Works • The scintillator: A block of plastic scintillator (cast PVT, or a surplus offcut) emits a brief flash of blue light when a charged particle deposits energy crossing it. A single muon produces only a few hundred to a few thousand photons — faint and fast, lasting nanoseconds. • Silicon photomultiplier (SiPM): A SiPM is an array of avalanche photodiodes biased just above breakdown, giving enormous gain (around 106) — enough to turn a handful of photons into a measurable current pulse. It replaces the bulky, high-voltage photomultiplier tubes of old with a 6 mm chip running on about 29 V. • Precise bias + temperature: A SiPM's gain is steeply sensitive to bias voltage and temperature, so a stable, low-noise bias supply (a quiet boost converter plus filtering) is critical. Drift the voltage and your count rate drifts with it — which is why real systems add temperature compensation. • Fast amplifier: A transimpedance or voltage amplifier with enough bandwidth (tens of MHz) converts the SiPM's fast current spike into a clean voltage pulse without smearing it. Layout matters here — short traces, good grounding, and supply bypassing keep noise below the tiny signal. • Discrimination and counting: A comparator fires when a pulse exceeds a threshold set just above the noise floor, producing a clean digital tick per event. An MCU counts ticks and shows the muon rate on an OLED. Add a second detector and require coincidence — only count when both fire at once — to reject electrical noise and confirm real through-going particles. // Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

Aislamiento de Vibraciones: Emplear 'dampers' o arandelas de silicona suave en los 4 puntos de anclaje de la placa del sensor para filtrar armónicos de alta frecuencia provocados por motores o ventiladores.

Orientación Geométrica: Alinear el eje X del sensor serigrafiado en la placa con el vector de avance del dispositivo. Una desviación angular de tan solo 2° introduce un error de deriva de aceleración cruzada.

troubleshooting.symptom: El microcontrolador no detecta el módulo o el bus se bloquea de forma intermitente.

troubleshooting.cause: Pico de corriente transitorio (inrush current) que provoca una caída momentánea del voltaje por debajo de 2.7V en el regulador.

troubleshooting.symptom: Reinicio espontáneo del microcontrolador (Brown-out Reset) al activarse actuadores o transmisores RF.

troubleshooting.cause: Acoplamiento capacitivo o inductivo generado por cables de motor PWM que discurren en paralelo a las líneas de datos de señal débil.
troubleshooting.fix: Separar físicamente los cables de potencia de los cables de señal al menos 3 cm, o utilizar cable apantallado con la malla conectada a masa sólo en un extremo.
troubleshooting.symptom: La señal del sensor muestra oscilaciones caóticas o ruido de alta frecuencia.

troubleshooting.cause: Variación térmica en el sensor no compensada o presencia de masa magnética ferrosa cercana (tornillos de acero cerca del magnetómetro).
troubleshooting.fix: Reemplazar tornillos de acero por tornillos de latón o nylon amagnéticos, y activar la compensación térmica por software en el firmware.
troubleshooting.symptom: Desviación continua (drift) en la lectura acumulada en reposo.

officialData.jobMapping: wearables and consumer health-device engineering — smartwatch, fitness-tracker, and ring companies.
officialData.safety: . It is not a medical instrument. Real SpO₂ readings require empirical calibration against a clinical reference on actual subjects — a number your build cannot produce trustworthily. Never make a health decision from it, and if you are worried about your heart or breathing, see a doctor, not a breadboard. reading the body — a Build List field guide 2 / 20 --- PAGE 3 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand photoplethysmography, separating a small AC signal riding on a large DC baseline, band-pass filtering, peak detection, and why motion artifacts dominate wearable sensing — the core of consumer health-device engineering.
officialData.whyThisMatters: The gentlest way into biosignals uses no electrodes at all. Shine light into tissue and a photodiode sees it dim slightly with every heartbeat, because each pulse of blood absorbs a little more. That is photoplethysmography (PPG) — the exact sensor on the back of every smartwatch and fitness ring. A $5 module gives you a raw optical waveform; your job is to pull the tiny pulsatile component out of a big steady one, filter it, and count peaks into a heart rate. It teaches the AC-on-DC structure that runs through every biosignal in this guide, without ever touching a skin electrode.

officialData.jobMapping: medical-device and precision-analog engineering — patient-monitoring, diagnostics, and analog front-end teams.
officialData.safety: , ALWAYS — AND NEVER INJECT CURRENT Anything wired to your skin must run on batteries and must never be connected to mains- powered gear (a plugged-in laptop, a bench scope, a wall adapter) while electrodes are on a body. Use series resistors in every electrode lead, and isolate (Bluetooth, or an unplugged battery laptop) if you need to see the data on a computer. Everything in this guide only measures — never build anything that pushes current into a person, and do not attach electrodes to anyone with a pacemaker or implanted device. reading the body — a Build List field guide 5 / 20 --- PAGE 6 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand instrumentation-amplifier topology, common-mode rejection (CMRR), driven- reference (right-leg drive) circuits, electrode half-cell offsets and why you must AC- couple, gain staging, and mains-hum rejection — the foundation of all precision biomedical analog design.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Your body produces electrical signals measured in millivolts — and it also acts as an antenna that picks up the mains hum flooding every room, often a thousand times larger than the signal you want. The instrumentation amplifier is the circuit that solves this: it amplifies only the difference between two electrodes while rejecting everything they see in common. Add a driven-reference electrode and careful filtering and suddenly a heartbeat or a muscle twitch emerges from the noise. This is the single circuit that makes ECG, EMG, and EEG possible, and building it yourself — rather than buying a module — is what separates people who understand biosignals from people who plug in a breakout board.

// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

It can show you a waveform and a heart rate; it cannot tell you whether your heart is healthy, and a normal-looking trace means nothing clinically. Never make a health decision from it. officialData.whatThisProves: You understand cardiac electrophysiology at the signal level, lead configurations, the ECG bandwidth, R-peak detection algorithms, heart-rate and HRV extraction, and safe patient-connected design — the exact skill set of medical-device and patient-monitoring engineering.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Every beat of your heart is a coordinated electrical wave, and it is large enough to read from your skin. Put two electrodes across your chest or arms, run them into a biopotential front end, and the classic PQRST complex appears on screen: the small P wave as the atria fire, the sharp QRS spike as the ventricles contract, the broad T wave as they reset. Then detect those R peaks and you have a live heart rate and beat-to-beat variability. It is the most iconic biosignal there is, the payoff is unmistakable, and it is the project that proves you can build precision analog that works on a living system.

// Firmware Receptor & Decodificador SDR (Python / GNU Radio)
import sys
import numpy as np
from rtlsdr import RtlSdr

sdr = RtlSdr()
sdr.sample_rate = 2.4e6    # 2.4 MSPS tasa de muestreo
sdr.center_freq = 1090e6   # Frecuencia transpondedor ADS-B (1090 MHz)
sdr.gain = 44.5            # Ganancia LNA en dB

print(f"[RADIO] Sintonizado en {sdr.center_freq / 1e6} MHz con ganancia {sdr.gain} dB.")

try:
    while True:
        # Lectura de muestras complejas I/Q (In-phase / Quadrature)
        samples = sdr.read_samples(256 * 1024)
        # Cálculo de potencia espectral instantánea (Magnitud IQ)
        magnitude = np.abs(samples)
        peak = np.max(magnitude)
        
        # Detección de preámbulo de pulso (Mode S squitter)
        if peak > 0.85:
            print(f"[ALERTA RF] Pulso detectado: Pico {peak:.2f} | Muestras > umbral: {np.sum(magnitude > 0.7)}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    sdr.close()
    print("[RADIO] Transceptor cerrado correctamente.")

officialData.whyThisMatters: When you contract a muscle, hundreds of motor units fire and their summed action potentials reach the skin as surface EMG — a burst of noisy, high-frequency activity whose amplitude tracks how hard you are pushing. It is the biosignal most useful as an interface, and it is the direct prerequisite for the myoelectric hand in project 5.

officialData.safety: — a rhythm that appears when your eyes close and disappears when they open — is the realistic and honest goal. Anything claiming to read thoughts or emotions from a few electrodes is overselling. Most hobby “brainwave” projects are actually detecting jaw clenching or eye blinks; the eyes-closed alpha test is how you prove yours is real. This is also not a diagnostic device, and it cannot tell you anything about your neurological health. reading the body — a Build List field guide 17 / 20 --- PAGE 18 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You can design a genuinely low-noise, high-gain analog front end, manage shielding and grounding at the microvolt level, distinguish real neural signal from muscle and eye artifact, and validate a result experimentally. Microvolt-level analog design and honest artifact rejection are precisely what neurotech teams look for.
officialData.whyThisMatters: EEG is the hardest biosignal there is: tens of microvolts, a hundred times smaller than an ECG, buried under mains hum, muscle tension, and eye movement. But there is one effect a careful DIY rig can genuinely capture — the alpha rhythm. Relax with your eyes closed and an 8 to 12 Hz oscillation appears over the back of your head; open your eyes and it vanishes within a second. Watching that band power rise and fall on an FFT, on command, is the most demanding and most rewarding build in this guide — and it is a real, reproducible neuroscience result, not a gimmick.

// Firmware de Captura & Renderizado para Visor NoIR
import cv2
import time
from picamera2 import Picamera2

picam2 = Picamera2()
config = picam2.create_video_configuration(main={"size": (800, 600), "format": "XBGR8888"})
picam2.configure(config)

# Ajuste para sensibilidad ultra-baja en luz infrarroja
picam2.set_controls({
    "AnalogueGain": 16.0,          # Ganancia analógica máxima
    "ExposureTime": 33333,         # 33ms (30 FPS estables)
    "AwbEnable": False,            # Desactivar balance de blancos automático
    "ColourGains": (1.0, 1.0)
})

picam2.start()
cv2.namedWindow("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN)
cv2.setWindowProperty("NightVision", cv2.WND_PROP_FULLSCREEN, cv2.WINDOW_FULLSCREEN)

print("[SISTEMA] Visor nocturno activo. Presiona 'q' para salir.")
while True:
    frame = picam2.capture_array()
    # Procesamiento para maximizar contraste en oscuridad
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    clahe = cv2.createCLAHE(clipLimit=3.0, tileGridSize=(8, 8))
    enhanced = clahe.apply(gray)
    cv2.imshow("NightVision", enhanced)
    if cv2.waitKey(1) & 0xFF == ord('q'):
        break

picam2.stop()
cv2.destroyAllWindows()

officialData.safety: . Use only low-power Class 1 / 2 modules (a few mW), never look into the beam or aim it at anyone, and remember infrared lasers are invisible — you cannot tell they are on. Set beams below eye level and keep this in mind for every build in this guide. seeing with light — a Build List field guide 2 / 18 --- PAGE 3 ---
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand photodiode and phototransistor detection, turning a light level into a clean logic edge with a comparator, microsecond-scale timing on a microcontroller, and converting a time interval into a physical measurement — the core of optical sensing and instrumentation.
officialData.whyThisMatters: The simplest thing you can do with light is notice when it stops arriving. Point a laser at a photodiode and you have a beam; break it and a voltage collapses in microseconds. Put two beams a known distance apart, time how long an object takes to cross from one to the other, and you have a speed trap — clock a Nerf dart, a dropped ball, a swinging door. It is the cheapest possible photonics build, the response is instant and visual, and it teaches the photodetection front end that every later project in this guide depends on.

officialData.jobMapping: autonomous vehicles, robotics, and LiDAR engineering — AV companies, robotics firms, and LiDAR sensor makers (a direct companion to radar roles). seeing with light — a Build List field guide 5 / 18
officialData.safety: Desconectar la alimentación antes de modificar el cableado. Verificar ausencia de cortocircuitos entre 3.3V y GND con multímetro antes de energizar.
officialData.whatThisProves: You understand time-of-flight ranging, the difference between direct (pulsed) and indirect (phase) ToF, why timing light is hard, signal-to-noise and averaging, and the I2C sensor integration real perception systems are built on. LiDAR is one of the hottest hiring areas in EE right now.
officialData.whyThisMatters: Radar measures distance with radio; LiDAR does it with light. A time-of-flight sensor fires a pulse of infrared light, measures how long it takes to bounce back, and multiplies by the speed of light to get range — millimetre-accurate, dozens of times a second. Building one around a module like the VL53L1X gets you a working laser rangefinder in an afternoon, and understanding what it does underneath — pulse timing versus phase, the speed of light, photon statistics — is the foundation of every autonomous-vehicle and robotics perception stack. This is the headline build, and it feeds straight into the scanner in project 3.
